A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SWAP research work. Text, equations, figures, tables and Appendices A–F are readable and support reliable matching across the revision.

before.justification: v3 reports original benchmark experiments, ablations, scaling and efficiency analyses, and fine-grained MATH500 results.

after.justification: v4 retains those experiments and adds original graph-construction measurements, training ablations, baseline results and qualitative examples.

M1.justification: Algorithms 1–2 replace v3's decreasing candidate budget b with a fixed selection width B and a separate increasing completion counter b. This changes the stated search procedure beyond renaming functions. The architecture, DM, CR and training remain unchanged; implementation changes or experimental reruns are not established.

E1.justification: Both versions use GSM8K, MATH/MATH500, FOLIO, ReClor, HumanEval and MBPP. The new FOLIO audit measures the existing graph-construction task, and the added GSM8K examples reuse an existing problem. No new dataset, domain or input scenario is introduced.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds SC (SFT-CoT@maj32) for both base models on math and logic benchmarks; the previous self-consistency baseline is retained as SC (CoT@maj32). New Table 3 includes few-shot, few-shot CoT and SFT-CoT graph comparisons. Appendix F adds ToT and RAP qualitative comparisons.

E3.justification: Section 4.4 introduces manual evaluation of 100 randomly selected FOLIO samples with LLaMA3-8B-Instruct, graph-producing baseline outputs, and node, dependency, graph and answer accuracy metrics. Table 2 adds training controls. Existing benchmark splits, rollout budgets, temperatures and step limits remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v4 substantially expands mechanism testing through direct graph-quality evaluation and error analysis in Section 4.4, plus no-SFT and no-training-structure ablations in Table 2. The earlier structure ablation is retained as inference-only. Appendix F adds ToT/RAP examples examining failures on the existing GSM8K case.

E5.justification: Retained Table 1 uncertainty values and Figure 4 bands are unchanged; the added self-consistency rows follow the existing plus/minus reporting practice. v4 adds no run or seed counts, confidence-interval procedure, significance tests or annotator-agreement reporting.

E6.justification: v4 adds self-consistency and training-ablation results, graph-error findings, comparator outputs, and direct graph-quality measurements, including SWAP's 90.0% joint-node and 68.0% whole-graph accuracy in Table 3. Previous numerical results remain unchanged. Table 3's 81.0% FOLIO answer accuracy uses 100 samples and is not a same-setting improvement over Table 1's 79.2%.

T1.justification: Section 4.4 newly defines joint-node correctness through simultaneous content and dependency correctness, whole-graph correctness through correctness of every node, and averaging of node proportions across graphs. These are limited additions to metric definitions; the existing formalism, Equations 1–8 and Appendix A mathematics are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution bullets and conclusion retain the same claims about structure-aware planning, accurate world modelling, DM/CR and superiority across reasoning benchmarks. The added experiments support these claims without changing their scope.

C2.justification: v4 qualifies graph reliability through its discussion of longer contexts and failed trajectories. It interprets the new ablations as evidence for high-quality training trajectories and structured training, and contrasts SWAP's reasoning with ToT misinterpretations and RAP inconsistencies. The standalone Limitations section is unchanged.

D1.justification: Section 4.4 documents output and prompting requirements for the new graph comparison: unchanged problem inputs, Dalvi-style graphs plus answers, and rationale-first generation for CoT settings. Existing appendix prompts, training and retrieval details, and the code/data access statement remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v4 adds Cao et al. (2025), Ni et al. (2024), He et al. (2024) and Jia et al. (2025) to the introduction and references. These modestly broaden citations around formal, program-based and structured reasoning; the Related Work section and central novelty positioning remain unchanged.

P1.justification: Localized rewrites expand the framework explanation, rename pseudocode functions and clarify answer extraction. A graph-evaluation subsection is inserted, and the ablation, efficiency and appendix discussions expand. The overall narrative order and most existing prose are retained.

P2.justification: v4 adds Table 3, expands Tables 1–2 and revises table headers. Figure 2 changes labels, including SemEquiv-LoRA to Rephrase-LoRA, and expands its caption. Other figures remain unchanged; table renumbering, reflow and additional boxed examples preserve the existing presentation style.

improvement.justification: The graph audit and added training controls strengthen evidence for SWAP's central claims beyond v3's final-answer comparisons. The gains are bounded by the small, single-model graph study and undocumented annotator agreement. A localized drawback is that the revised fixed-width pseudocode can overshoot B completed paths without triggering its b=B stopping check, tempering the overall improvement.
